original_value: Bin-picking of small parcels and other textureless planar-faced objects is a common task at warehouses. A general color image–based vision-guided robot picking system requires feature extraction and goal image preparation of various objects. However, feature extraction for goal image matching is difficult for textureless objects. Further, prior preparation of huge numbers of goal images is impractical at a warehouse. In this paper, we propose a novel depth image–based vision-guided robot bin-picking system for textureless planar-faced objects. Our method uses a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) model that is trained on 15,000 annotated depth images synthetically generated in a physics simulator to directly predict grasp points without object segmentation. Unlike previous studies that predicted grasp points for a robot suction hand with only one vacuum cup, our DCNN also predicts optimal grasp patterns for a hand with two vacuum cups (left cup on, right cup on, or both cups on). Further, we propose a surface feature descriptor to extract surface features (center position and normal) and refine the predicted grasp point position, removing the need for texture features for vision-guided robot control and sim-to-real modification for DCNN model training. Experimental results demonstrate the efficiency of our system, namely that a robot with 7 degrees of freedom can pick randomly posed textureless boxes in a cluttered environment with a 97.5% success rate at speeds exceeding 1000 pieces per hour.

result.paraphrase: Bin-picking small parcels and other textureless planar-faced objects is a routine warehouse task. Conventional color image–based vision-guided robot picking systems need feature extraction and goal-image preparation for diverse objects, but textureless items make goal-image matching difficult and precomputing vast numbers of goal images impractical in warehouses. This paper presents a new depth image–based vision-guided robot bin-picking system for textureless planar-faced objects. The method employs a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) trained on 15,000 annotated depth images synthetically produced in a physics simulator to predict grasp points directly without object segmentation. Unlike earlier work that predicted grasp points for a suction hand with only one vacuum cup, our DCNN also predicts the best grasp pattern for a hand with two vacuum cups, with the left cup on, the right cup on, or both cups on. We also propose a surface feature descriptor that extracts surface features, namely center position and normal, and refines the predicted grasp point, eliminating the need for texture features in vision-guided robot control and for sim-to-real adjustment during DCNN training. Experiments show the system’s efficiency: a 7-degree-of-freedom robot can pick randomly posed textureless boxes in a cluttered environment with a 97.5% success rate at over 1000 pieces per hour.
